chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it, said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, obligated the Jihad and magnified it, and made it His victory and His helper. By Allah! Neither the world nor the Religion can be correct except by it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Jihad in establishing both worldly and religious order according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) underscores Jihad as the foundational pillar for the rectification of both the temporal and spiritual realms, linking divine victory directly to its practice. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that Jihad is not merely military but a comprehensive mechanism for establishing justice and divine order. The emphasis on 'magnifying' its status highlights its elevated rank among acts of worship in the tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, raising it, said,

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Obligated the Jihad and Magnified it, and Made it as His<sup>azwj</sup> Victory and His<sup>azwj</sup> Helper. By Allah<sup>azwj</sup>! Neither the world nor the Religion can be correct except by it’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Mahbub in a marfu’ the following: “

Amir al-Mu’minin, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has made Jihad obligatory, considered it great and has made it His victory (support) and supporter. By Allah, the worldly affairs as well as religious affairs are never enhanced without Jihad.”
